steps.content: Early February, N.F. 114
After that, things keep going surprisingly smoothly.

Due to security concerns and to keep your cover identity as the "fan club president," you can't discuss sensitive technical subjects with "Archivist 19260817," yet your communication has continued constantly.
Rather than research topics, they seem more interested in DisCity lore, and are especially fascinated by stories of Chief's adventures.

When they ask about Chief's recent activities, you cherry-pick a few headline stories and attach some blurry "snapshots." When they're curious about Chief's past, you share some half-true media stories to satisfy their curiosity.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I heard Chief personally interrogates Sinners? Is that true?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: More or less.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Is he really as... invincible as the rumors say? Is he really that resourceful?
steps.female_content:
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I heard Chief personally interrogates Sinners? Is that true?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: More or less.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Is she really as... invincible as the rumors say? Is she really that resourceful?

steps.content: You give an affirmative answer and also helpfully make up quite a few details as evidence. Watching the "typing..." notification flash repeatedly above the chat box with no new text appearing, you can't help but laugh out loud.
You can almost picture them on the other side of the screen, eyebrows furrowed in disbelief, fingers hovering hesitantly over the keyboard before finally cautiously typing out a response.
Gradually, your conversations extend beyond discussions of Chief and research, as Archivist begins voluntarily sharing tiny details of their daily life.

For instance, when equipment readings suddenly spiked during an experiment last month, Archivist got so excited thinking they'd made a breakthrough that they even drafted an outline for a paper. But moments later, they discovered it was only caused by a loose connection.
And two weeks ago, they spent forty-eight hours in the lab trying to verify a hypothesis. Having forgotten to eat, they ended up fainting from low blood sugar.

Mysterious tiny paw prints on lab reports, new buds sprouting on the windowsill, a sudden rush of inspiration... whether it's moments of happiness or frustration, or even just some insignificant feelings, you seem to be the first person they talk to when something happens.
Before you realize it, you've come to know many things they like.
You know that when they leave the lab, they prefer to eat alone at a café on the street corner.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Whenever I'm done with the experiment, I go there and sit for a while. From that corner seat, I can watch the sunset through the window. It's like a burning, orange ball of fire. It's beautiful.
You know that in their spare time, they like to reorganize all their documents and books in the most practical order.
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Today I reorganized all my documents again. After sorting them by category, they're much easier to find now.
You know they love the aroma of freshly brewed herbal tea. They say the rising steam makes them think of flower fields in spring.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I always brew a cup of herbal tea when I'm doing my reading. The aroma helps me concentrate.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I've never actually seen a real flower field, but I imagine it must be as dewy and vibrant as the steamy, freshly brewed herbal tea.
Then a few days ago, they suddenly sent you a photo.

It's a small white flower defiantly emerging from a crevice in the rock. A slender finger gently caresses the blossom, its delicate petals unfurling in the desolate crack, looking so lonely yet remarkably resilient.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Remember the herbal tea I told you about? This is what it's made from.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Someone suggested picking it to make tea, but after thinking about it, I refused.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Blooming from a rock is way cooler than becoming a cup of tea, don't you think?

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: You're always sharing photos with me, so I thought I'd send one to you today.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I hope it cheers you up a little.
That day, when you drag your exhausted body back to the Bureau after finishing a field assignment, the moon is already high in the night sky.
You rest on the couch for a moment, then pull your device from your pocket and log onto the dark web as usual. You find an unread message in your inbox.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I heard Chief has been out on missions lately?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Yeah. I went along too. Could barely keep up.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Haven't received many messages from you these past couple of days. Have you been busy as well?
You've just set down your device to get ready for bed when the screen lights up again, the reply popping up almost instantly.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Recently... there have been some changes to my research project, requiring more of my attention. I'm managing well enough.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: What about you? Have you been out taking photos again?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Something like that. Though things were so chaotic today I nearly took a fall and almost smashed my camera.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: No way?! That sounds dangerous! Are you alright? You're not hurt, are you?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Don't worry, I'm fine. All the photos are saved. I'll pick out some good ones, touch them up a bit, and pack them into a zip file.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Pack them?

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Like when I group my experimental records?
These weird comparisons always put a smile on your face. Archivist is such a nerd, but inexplicably, that's kind of cute.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Yes, think of it as some kind of research record.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Just like you said, categorizing and organizing them makes everything easier to find later.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I see, that's an interesting way to put it.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...If I ever get the chance, I'd like to visit DisCity myself. To see where you live, and all those scenic spots you've mentioned.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Perhaps... I might even have the opportunity to meet that legendary Chief, together with you.
The yearning in their words reaches you through the cold screen, and you can clearly feel the sincerity behind.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: In that case, I sincerely extend an invitation to you. You have the welcome of DisCity and the MBCC.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Are you speaking on behalf of Chief's fan club?
You smile and gently type out a reply.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: On behalf of the fan club, but also myself.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: You're welcome in DisCity. Once your project wraps up, I'll throw a celebration party for you.

They quickly respond with a smiling emoji and say nothing more. As the chat falls still, you lean back against the couch and swipe your fingertips across the screen, switching to another conversation.
<color=#fb9259>9th</color>: Chief, the tracking report from the tech department is ready.

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: Any findings?

<color=#fb9259>9th</color>: The signal source has been located on the outskirts of DisCity, in a small satellite town. It's primarily an agricultural production area with almost no unusual activities.

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: ...Understood. Continue monitoring.
You stare at the report from the 9th Agency. Everything appears harmless. Nothing is out of the ordinary. It's almost surprising, and it raises your suspicions.
From your interactions so far, you've already formed a mental image of this mysterious "independent scientist."

<size=50>A young girl</size> under twenty years old　　<size=40>Perhaps just of age?</size>
　　　　　<size=50>Privileged background</size>　Have received top education
　　　　　　　　　　　Intelligent　Almost a <size=50>genius</size>
　　　　　　　　Small social circle　　Seems to have <size=50>few friends</size>
　　　　　　　　<size=50>Research scholar</size>　Passionate about her work
　　　　　　　　　　　<size=40>Inexperienced</size>　　<size=40>Immature</size>　　<size=40>Just starting out</size>
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　...
　　　　　　　　　　　　　Independent?　　<size=50>Lonely?</size>
You stare blankly at the screen until it goes dark, then instinctively tap to wake it.

"Archivist 19260817" seems to be nothing more than an ordinary girl sitting before a screen, playfully joking with you, the two of you separated by thousands of kilometers yet connected by data between two worlds.
She still skitters around certain topics. She's never revealed her location or the specifics of her research, yet she is eager to share anything outside of these subjects.
Those restrained, polite texts are like a cautiously extended hand—yearning for connection and conversation, yet hesitant of complete honesty. Is this truly a trap, or perhaps...
...you're lonely enough to entrust all your thoughts and feelings to a stranger on the dark web?
A message notification interrupts your thoughts. A long block of text suddenly appears in the chat window.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Have you...

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Have you ever considered that maybe... you could distance yourself a bit from him, from ${PlayerName}?
steps.female_content:
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Have you...

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Have you ever considered that maybe... you could distance yourself a bit from her, from ${PlayerName}?

steps.content:
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Don't get me wrong! I'm not trying to speak ill of Chief. It's just that you're always chasing after him. It must be exhausting for you too.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I just want you to be more mindful of your own safety.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: He's always risking his life in the most dangerous places, resolving those terrifying crises. But you're just an ordinary person... I don't want you to get caught in the crossfire and get hurt.
steps.female_content:
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Don't get me wrong! I'm not trying to speak ill of Chief. It's just that you're always chasing after her. It must be exhausting for you too.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I just want you to be more mindful of your own safety.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: She's always risking her life in the most dangerous places, resolving those terrifying crises. But you're just an ordinary person... I don't want you to get caught in the crossfire and get hurt.

steps.content:
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: But I also understand that all those obstacles are not a reason to give up. Just like I wouldn't give up on my experiments easily.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: So, it's okay. My experiments often go wrong too, but if you persist, you'll eventually find the problem and reach the solution...

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...
The "typing..." message keeps flashing at the top of the chat window, but the next message never arrives.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: What's wrong?

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...Nothing.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I've just... run into some trouble lately. Makes me wonder sometimes...

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Will I ever truly find the answer if I keep going...?
Hmm...?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: You sound a bit sad?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Is something troubling you? If you'd like to talk about it, I'm here to listen.
A reply pops up quickly. But just as you make out the first few characters, the message is immediately deleted.

After a moment, she responds with just a brief "thank you," then subtly changes the subject. You don't press further, simply following along with some trivial updates. When it's finally late enough into the night, you say "good night" to each other.

You set down your device and finish your nighttime routine. Then you return to your room, turn off the lights, and lie down in bed. The room is silent and it's all dark out. Only the sound of your own breathing fills the air.
Just as you're about to close your eyes in the darkness, the device on your bedside suddenly lights up, the cold white glow jarring in the quiet night.
It's a lengthy message. This time, she doesn't delete it.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...I'm sorry. You were clearly just concerned about me, yet I behaved so rudely.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I don't know who I should share this with, or if I should share it at all... It's not about my research, but my... family.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: My family has always been strict and demanding with me. "With great ability comes great responsibility"—that's been drilled into me since childhood. My father was harsh, and my mother constantly reminded me that as the youngest child, I had to work even harder to be the best and never be outshone.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: My older siblings are all exceptional, and very... independent. They've never seemed unsure about anything. I've always wanted to prove myself too, to show everyone that I'm not just a spare.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I tried so hard to adapt, pushed myself to my limits, but honestly... it was exhausting. I was afraid I might never measure up to my family's standards.
Her messages appear line by line with brief pauses, still somewhat cautious.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Later, someone I deeply respected returned to my life. He told me I didn't have to follow in my siblings' footsteps, that I should pursue the research I enjoyed, as long as I believed it was meaningful.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: It was he who introduced me to new knowledge, who supported me, protected me, and guided me. He led me beyond the confines of my family home into a larger world, where I met people completely different from myself.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: My research truly made a difference, and for the first time, I received gratitude from others. It was the first time I felt needed. He told me this was my way of fulfilling my "responsibility."

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: That's how it should have been, but...
Her messages keep flooding in, the struggle, hesitation, and weariness palpable between the lines. You wait patiently, while an inexplicable unease wells up inside you.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: But recently, I've discovered some things that seem to deviate from the truth I once believed in.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...Did I make a mistake? If I was wrong, how could I face the people who placed their trust in me? How can I verify the truth? And how can I possibly make amends?
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Can I... truly fulfill my responsibility? Can I really help everyone?
Though she's inadvertently revealing information that warrants further clarification, right now, you're more concerned about her feelings.
Her heart lies shattered, revealing her pain. For the first time, she's opened herself up to you completely. And for the first time, she's seeking your advice. How should you respond?

options: Encourage her to talk to more people
Encourage her not to overburden herself

choices.text: Encourage her to talk to more people
Encourage her not to overburden herself

steps.content:
<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: It took a lot of courage just to say all this. Thank you for sharing it with me.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: You've been carrying this burden alone for too long. Have you considered talking to someone you trust? It might help.
After a long pause, you finally receive her reply.
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...No. I can't tell anyone. Even with you, I can't say anything more. I'm sorry.

options: Encourage her not to overburden herself

choices.text: Encourage her not to overburden herself

steps.content:
<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: That's alright. I won't force you. I just want you to know that you've worked hard enough and done well enough. You don't need to shoulder everything alone.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Have you considered that perhaps these overwhelming responsibilities and expectations shouldn't have been yours to bear in the first place?

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...I can't.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: If I let go of them, then I'd truly be nothing.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Have you considered that perhaps these overwhelming responsibilities and expectations shouldn't have been yours to bear in the first place?

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...I can't.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: If I let go of them, then I'd truly be nothing.
You gaze at the unyielding response on your screen and sigh, beginning to type your reply.
<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Alright then. Don't let go. Keep going.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: "No matter what others may say, you are a remarkable researcher. You don't work for fame or fortune. You're always proud of your research and are reverent toward it. You use your knowledge to fight against disasters and to save lives..."

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: "This dedication alone is something to be proud of, and worthy of everyone's admiration."

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: "Scientists are always fumbling in the dark... No, I believe the same goes for everyone who tries hard in their lives. We all put up a facade in public, but behind that, we all struggle just as clumsily."

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: "Even ${PlayerName} is the same. I've seen it countless times already. He's struggling all the time. He makes mistakes and feels lost too. He's hardly as cool as you think he is."
steps.female_content: "Even ${PlayerName} is the same. I've seen it countless times already. She's struggling all the time. She makes mistakes and feels lost too. She's hardly as cool as you think she is."

steps.content: There's no reply from the other side, but you know she's reading. After a brief pause, you take a deep breath and send your final message.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: So...

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: You shouldn't give up either. As long as you keep believing, you'll find your answer.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Whatever the outcome, I'll be right beside you.

Meanwhile
Furor, Farlands
The lab is cold and silent this late at night, with only the faint glow of the screen illuminating Hypatia's face.
She stares at that message coming from the distant DisCity in a daze. After a long while, she finally can't help but let out a soft chuckle, murmuring to herself.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Number one fan, huh? What kind of fan criticizes their idol like that...
...Click. A sound behind her interrupts her mutter.
Hypa, still haven't gone to bed? Working so late on your research... you're really pushing yourself too hard.

The smile on the girl's face instantly freezes as she stiffly turns to look behind her. From the darkness, a tall figure saunters into the room, stepping into the light. His smile appears gentle, yet his eyes flash with an unreadable gleam.
Hypatia steadies her voice, casually turning to one side to block the screen with her body.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...Just wanted to review the research materials once more.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: I know you're working hard, but still, you shouldn't neglect your rest. I don't get to visit you often, and I'd be heartbroken if you worked yourself sick.
A hand gently rests on Hypatia's head, just as it used to when she was a child, softly stroking the top of her head.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Plus...

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: I received a warning from a distant friend. She said you might be in danger.
Without warning, Hypatia is pulled aside, exposing the conversation on the screen behind her.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: That's...!

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Chatting with a friend from DisCity? I'm glad you made a new friend, little sister, but I'm worried about you. There are many dangerous people out there. What if DisCity's intelligence agency targets you? They're certainly not our friends, you know.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: I didn't leak anything confidential! I was just... contacting an informant.
Hypatia feigns composure, trying her best to conceal the truth.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Black Rings don't exist in farlands, but we can obtain Mania data from DisCity through the dark web. I've already gathered considerable intelligence through him, and perhaps later we could even...
steps.female_content: Black Rings don't exist in farlands, but we can obtain Mania data from DisCity through the dark web. I've already gathered considerable intelligence through her, and perhaps later we could even...

steps.content: Adelaide raises his hand slightly, and despite his soft smile, he cuts off her explanation firmly.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: I understand, of course. You've always been a genuine person, Hypa. I'm sure this informant is now a friend, right?
He pauses, his gaze gradually turning cold, though his voice remains gentle.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Such a shame, though. The intelligence I received says... that person you've been in contact with is none other than the MBCC's Chief.
A message notification chimes from behind. The screen instantly glitches, the texts distorting before reorganizing to reveal several new lines.

<color=#b0e7b4>Dev: Fixed it.

Dev: I've modified her IP address. They won't be able to trace it for now.

Dev: Still, be careful. I'm too busy these days to have time to clean up more messes here.</color>

<color=#b0e7b4>Dev: To prepare for our next phase, I'm going to investigate those "rats" who've snuck into Fraser City.
Dev: Watch your sister. Tell her to stay out of trouble and not get caught.</color>
Hypatia's face turns deathly pale. The male voice near her ear is as gentle as it is cold, like a venomous snake coiled around her neck.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Think about it. Why did he contact you using a fake identity? Just to make friends? Or... did he know who you were right from the start, and was just baiting you with Mania intelligence?
steps.female_content: Think about it. Why did she contact you using a fake identity? Just to make friends? Or... did she know who you were right from the start, and was just baiting you with Mania intelligence?

steps.content: She can't utter another word. Adelaide's smile remains unchanged as he places his hand on Hypatia's shoulder, giving it two light pats as if to reassure her.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Sincerity and kindness. Our Hypa's best qualities.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Someone has taken advantage of that... But don't worry, you simply need guidance. With me here, everything shall be taken care of.
Though his palm is warm, it feels like a pair of shackles digging into her shoulder, sending a chill that reaches her bones.
A gentleness that's almost indulging. A closeness that suffocates.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Don't worry, Hypa... Just like always...

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Your brother will always be by your side.
